device_power_w.method: Incremental power attributable to active browsing with the screen on, per device type chosen by the user. Provisional engineering ranges, not validated population averages; no reliable data on the share of browsing time by device type. Watts are never inferred from the user agent.

network_kwh_per_gb.method: SWD v4 network intensity (310 TWh / 5.29 ZB). An allocation estimate, not a physical measurement: network energy is not proportional to data volume (Mytton et al. 2024). Range = sensitivity range for fixed networks; mobile networks not yet separated.

datacenter_kwh_per_gb.method: SWD v4 data-center intensity (290 TWh / 5.29 ZB). The SWD user-device segment (0.080) is NOT used: the device is computed from time to avoid double counting.

streaming_kwh_per_hour.method: Network + data center energy per hour of streaming (device energy is counted separately). Realistic average: about 0.077-0.08 kWh/h (IEA 2019 typical hour; research mid value for HD 0.08). The IEA figure is a TOTAL that includes the viewing device; for a phone on Wi-Fi in SD the IEA derives about 0.037 kWh/h, with more than 80% of it in data transmission. The reference used here (0.10 kWh/h for network + data center alone, plus the device) is therefore deliberately well above the realistic total, to err on the side of overestimation. Carbon Trust/DIMPACT (2021) gives about 55 gCO2e per hour for Europe as a total. Fraunhofer FAME (2024) recommends the kWh-per-hour metric. No universal value by resolution exists; per-resolution ranges in the research include the display device and are not used directly.

dc_share_of_remote.method: Share of 'network + data center' energy attributed to the data center when only a time-based total is available (streaming): 0.055 / (0.055 + 0.059), the SWD v4 ratio. Used only for the data-center water term.

ai_text_wh_per_prompt.method: Generic text prompt: cross-source reference of 0.30 Wh (Gemini median 0.24 Wh, comprehensive method; GPT-4o about 0.3 Wh, modelled by Epoch AI; ChatGPT average 0.34 Wh, methodology undisclosed). Long-context and reasoning requests can be far higher. Provider-specific values for Claude, Mistral and Llama not found.

ai_text_prompts_per_hour.method: The browser cannot see prompts, so a usage rate per hour of active session is assumed (product-design assumption, no industry measurement). It is used only for time not covered by per-service message counting (Settings, AI usage), which replaces it with real counts.

ai_image.method: No defensible energy per generated image: it depends on model, hardware and resolution and providers do not disclose it. Remote part not estimated (device and network are counted). Indicative research range 1.35-11.5 Wh per image (Luccioni et al.) is not used.

ai_video.method: No comparable provider-independent measurement of energy per generated second. Remote part not estimated (device and network are counted). Multiplying image energy by frame count would be incorrect.

streaming_uhd_gb_per_hour.method: Observed data rate (bytes transferred / active time) above which streaming is treated as 4K: Netflix reports about 7 GB/h for 4K and 3 GB/h for HD, and third-party sources put YouTube 1080p at roughly 1.5-4 GB/h and 4K at roughly 5 GB/h (no official figure found), so 4 GB/h separates them. The rate is only used to raise the estimate: lower rates stay at the reference. In practice the declared bytes of video are heavily undercounted (range requests are aborted and chunked responses declare no size), so this threshold rarely triggers.

streaming_uhd_factor.method: Multiplier on the streaming reference for 4K-level data rates. Ratio of the research mid values for 4K and HD (0.12 / 0.08).

unknown_response_kb.method: Average size assumed for each request whose server does not declare a size (typically compressed or chunked responses), so that sites that do not declare sizes are not counted as nearly free. Central value = HTTP Archive 2024 desktop median page weight over its median request count (2,652 KB / 71 requests = about 37 KB; mobile 2,311 / 66 = 35 KB). The real mix of undeclared responses is unknown (they are probably dynamic, compressed resources), hence the wide range. Applies to browsing categories (not to streaming or AI text, whose energy is time-based).

reference_thresholds_wh_per_day.method: Default traffic-light thresholds (green/yellow/red) expressed as daily energy, converted with the selected profile. Reference: about 8 h of laptop browsing at 12 W is 96 Wh before network and data-center energy. These are NOT scientific or regulatory thresholds: users can set their own.

onsite_l_per_kwh_dc.method: Direct cooling water of data centers (WUE): LBNL US estimate 0.36 L/kWh (0.30-0.48), Microsoft fleet 0.30 L/kWh in FY2024 and 0.27 in FY2025. Different facility populations and methods.

grid_l_per_kwh.method: Water consumed (not withdrawn) to generate electricity: US national average 4.52 L/kWh (LBNL, 2023). Country datasets for EU, Italy, China, Japan and world were not found: the US value is used as a proxy everywhere. Applied to all electricity (device, network, data center).

water_formula: water = data-center energy x on-site WUE + total energy x electricity water intensity (consumption, never withdrawal)
